data.location: Save A A A A view of Lotte Department Store. Lotte Department Store Department store stocks rallied across the board as expectations grew for expanding spending by foreign tourists and a recovery in high-end consumption. Analysts say the earnings improvement in the department store sector could extend beyond the year-end, with rising inbound spending compounded by domestic asset and income effects. Lotte Shopping (023530.KS) was trading at 119,800 won, up 7,500 won or 6.68% from the previous session, as of 2:24 p.m. on the 8th, according to the Korea Exchange. Hyundai Department Store (069960.KS) rose 4.50% to 102,100 won, while Shinsegae (004170.KS) gained 4.41% to 414,000 won. E-Mart (139480.KS) climbed 2.83%, Daegu Department Store (006370.KS) added 1.45% and Hanwha Galleria (452260.KS) edged up 1.05%. Foreign spending is the main driver lifting the sector. Tourism spending averaged 2.1 trillion won a month in the second quarter, up 59.6% from a year earlier, as the exchange rate, per-capita spending by foreign visitors and the number of arrivals all improved. Department stores, which draw a large share of revenue from luxury goods and fashion, are seen as a direct beneficiary channel of the inbound spending boom. Shinsegae is expected to see the gains concentrated at its main store in Myeong-dong. iM Securities estimates net sales to foreign customers at the Shinsegae main store will rise 94.8% this year from a year earlier. The brokerage said the store's ability to capture foreign spending has strengthened as a luxury-focused renovation combined with traffic drawn by its duty-free operations and digital signage. It projects Shinsegae's department store revenue at 3.02 trillion won this year, up 13.0%, with operating profit rising 37.7% to 559.3 billion won.
